section: Educational Psychology · Ch — Assessment, Evaluation & CCE
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A teacher uses a simple list of specific behaviours or skills (e.g., 'raises hand before speaking — Yes/No', 'brings homework — Yes/No') and marks only whether each one is present or absent for each student. This observation tool is called a:
explanation: A checklist records only the presence or absence of specific traits/behaviours (a simple Yes/No or tick), unlike a rating scale, which records the DEGREE to which a trait is present (e.g., on a 1-5 scale) rather than a binary judgement.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch — Assessment, Evaluation & CCE
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A teacher assesses a student's classroom participation using a scale from 1 (rarely participates) to 5 (always participates actively), indicating the DEGREE to which the trait is shown rather than simply its presence or absence. This observation tool is called a:
explanation: A rating scale captures the degree/intensity of a trait along a graded continuum — distinct from a checklist (simple Yes/No presence) or an anecdotal record (a narrative description of a specific observed incident).
